newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Hyundai faces crisis in steel mill plan.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Hyundai faces crisis in steel mill plan.

text.p: South Korea's trade ministry on Thursday said the country did not need another integrated steel mill, dealing a blow to Hyundai Group's plans to enter the steel industry with two blast furnaces.
The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy said in a statement construction of a new mill was "not desirable".

In July Hyundai said its unit, Inchon Iron and Steel Co KS, would build a mill capable of producing six million tonnes of steel a year by 2004. Inchon and other Hyundai affiliates now make steel products.
A new still mill would lead to an oversupply as domestic and foreign demand was unlikely to grow sharply in the future, the statement said.
It was not the first time the government has expressed opposition to an expansion of steel capacity, but it was the most definitive official statement so far.
The statement did not name Hyundai but was widely interpreted as being aimed at South Korea's largest industrial conglomerate, whose founder Chung Ju-yung wants a steel mill as his crowning ambition.
Hyundai has given no details of its steel mill plans, but analysts estimate it would cost at least 10 trillion won ($12.1 billion).
Industry analysts said Hyundai was not likely to abandon its ambitions in steel.
"I don't think today's remarks will eventually stop Hyundai from entering the sector," said Kim Gyung-jung at Daewoo Economic Research Institute.
"Hyundai has promoted the plan for a very long period. The current government's opposition will only delay the group's entry," he said.

Although the government cannot outright bar Hyundai from making steel, it could make life difficult for the conglomerate in a country where industry and the government work hand-in-hand and where the supply of credit is tightly controlled.
Seoul has given up controls on most private business activities, including steelmaking, but maintains restrictions on certain industries requiring foreign technology.
Hyundai has said it needs to make steel for its own companies, including carmaker Hyundai Motor Co and shipbuilder Hyundai Heavy Industries Co.
It has said demand from its affiliates would reach some six million tonnes, matching the output of the planned mill.
Pohang Iron and Steel Co is now the only South Korean company with an integrated steel mill.
Inchon plans to expand its existing plant to increase its overall annual capacity to 12 million tonnes of steel products in 2004 from the current 3.7 million.
